newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Public Bank to continue "foreign" shares.
newsitem.headline: Public Bank to continue "foreign" shares.

text.p: Malaysia's Public Bank Bhd (PBB) said it will continue to separately list the "foreign" tranche of its stock.
In a statement released over the weekend, the bank also said foreign investors "have always been allowed" to buy the local tranche of its stock.
"...PBB shares separately quoted as "foreign" on the main board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, will continue to be separately quoted as "foreign"".
The bank, Malaysia's fourth largest banking group, said it made the clarification in response to recent newspaper reports.

The company's foreign shares tumbled while its local shares surged last week, on market interpretations that the company was making about to make amendments to allow foreign investors to buy the local tranche of the stock.
There was also speculation that the foreign shares will be merged with the local shares.
But the bank said foreigners who could not buy the foreign shares when the 30 percent shareholding limit had been reached, had all along been allowed to buy the local tranche of the stock.

"When foreigners buy "local" shares (as the have always been allowed to) such "local" shares will still be credited into their CDS central depository system account (even if the company's maximum foreign shareholding limit of 30 percent has been reached)," the statement said.

But in order to comply with Malaysian regulations limiting foreign control of domestic banks to 30 percent, Public Bank said it has decided that local shares held by foreigners will not entitled to vote, though they are entitled to all other rights.

"The rationale for this is in order to limit control (which is exercised through the right to vote) by foreigners to within 30 percent in order for Public Bank to comply with its maximum foreign sharesholding limit," the statement said.
